metaDescription: Monitor CPU, memory, disk, network and battery on your Mac. Manage the native macOS charge limit and check optional AI usage limits.
notFoundDescription: The page you’re looking for doesn’t exist or has moved.
heroTitle: See what your Mac is doing.
heroLead: A native menu bar app for CPU, memory, disk, network, sensors and AI plan limits, with the macOS charge limit one click away.
releasePending: The public release is being prepared. Follow releases on GitHub.
processesTitle: Find what’s busy, or holding a port
batteryLead: Monny uses the charge limit built into macOS, the same setting as in Battery Settings. No helper, no root access.
batteryRequirement: Requires a Mac with a battery and macOS 26.4 or later. 100% turns the limit off. macOS may occasionally charge to 100% to keep battery estimates accurate.
aiTitle: AI plan limits next to CPU and memory
aiLead: Check what is left of your plan before a long task. Monny uses each tool’s own sign-in on this Mac and checks every 2 minutes while you look, every 5 minutes otherwise.
aiNote: Turn it on in Settings and pick your tools. Services that would need browser cookies, a pasted API key or a separate Monny account are not supported.
dashboardLead: History from 1 minute to 7 days, top processes and temperature sensors in one window.
privacyLead: No Monny account, analytics or telemetry. The charge limit is changed with your regular user permissions, without a helper or root access. Monny is open source under the MIT license.
installLead: Monny is free and available as a DMG from GitHub Releases.
installDetail2: Open the DMG and drag the icon
installDetail3: Once for each download, see below
noticeInline: Not notarized yet: the first launch needs one extra step.
drawerInstallLink: Not notarized yet · How to open
noticeTitle: Monny isn’t notarized by Apple yet
noticeDescription: Monny is signed, but has not yet been submitted to Apple for notarization. macOS may block the first launch. Allow the downloaded copy using one of the options below.
noticeQuote: Apple could not verify Monny is free of malware.
pasteCommand: Paste the command and press Return.
settingsStep1: Try opening Monny once, then dismiss the warning.
settingsStep3: Scroll to Security, choose Open Anyway and confirm.
noticeFootnote: Needed once for each download. Only allow a copy you downloaded from this project.
questionsLead: Something else? Open an issue or start a discussion on GitHub.
faqQ1: Why does macOS say it can’t verify Monny?
faqA1: Monny is signed but not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the first launch. Follow the installation guide above to allow the copy you downloaded from this project.
faqA2: Macs with Apple silicon running macOS 26 or later. The charge limit also needs a Mac with a battery and macOS 26.4 or later. Intel Macs aren’t supported.
faqQ3: Does Monny send my data anywhere?
faqA3: System readings stay on your Mac. Monny connects for updates and, if you enable AI limits, to the services you select using their tools’ existing sign-in.
faqQ4: Will the charge limit stay on after I quit Monny?
faqA4: Yes. macOS keeps its own limit after you quit Monny, through sleep and restarts. You can also change it in System Settings → Battery.
faqA5: Monny checks for signed updates with Sparkle and asks before installing them. You can turn automatic checks on or off and check manually in Settings.
faqA6: Yes. Monny is free and open source under the MIT license. No account, subscription or ads.

ctaLead: Free and open source. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

emptyDescription: Page not found. Check the address or return to the home page.
menuBarTitle: Readings right next to the clock
menuBarLead: Add CPU load, CPU temperature or battery level next to the Monny icon. Each one is off until you turn it on in Settings. A small dot on the icon appears when your Mac is hot or memory pressure is critical.
menuBarHint: Example readings. They update at the refresh rate you choose: every 1, 2 or 5 seconds.
readingsTitle: Quick while you look, quiet when you don’t
readingsLead: One shared sampler reads everything. While the popover, the dashboard or menu bar readings are showing, it runs at your refresh rate. Otherwise it reads every 10 seconds, enough for history and notifications.
popoverOpenDetail: Every 2 s · or 1 s, 5 s in Settings
thermalDetail: The CPU temperature chip turns amber at Fair and red at Serious or Critical.
samplingNote: Example timing with the default refresh rate.
sensorsNote: Sensors differ between Mac models. When one isn’t reported, Monny says so instead of showing zero or a guess.
processesLead: Search by name, PID or port. Type 3002 to see which of your processes listens on it and quit just that one. A process above 80% of one core for a minute or more shows up under Needs attention.
processesNote: Monny lists apps and processes running under your account. Force Quit asks first; Monny never ends a process on its own. Example values.
portHint: Open a row for CPU, memory, path, parent process and all its ports, then quit just that process. Monny looks again and tells you whether it quit, is still running or a new process took the port.
portNote: Only your own processes are readable, so Monny never claims a port is free for everyone. Example values.
powerNote: Example values. On battery Monny shows what the Mac draws and the time left that macOS estimates.
limitKeptNote: Change it any time in Monny or System Settings → Battery.
notificationsTitle: One alert when it matters, then quiet
notificationsLead: Choose the notifications you want in Settings. Each one is sent once per episode, so a long hot afternoon is one alert, not one every few seconds.
notifyBusyApp: An app keeps the Mac busy
notificationsNote: Checked items are on by default. Battery alerts appear only on Macs with a battery.
busyBody: Over {value} CPU for the last 5 minutes. Quit it if you don’t need it.
sentOnce: Sent once. If Xcode calms down and gets busy again later, that is a new alert.
sourceApi: The tool’s sign-in, then the service’s usage API
sourceLocal: Local IDE data, no network request
paceNote: The bar is quota left. The thin mark is time left in the window: a bar shorter than the mark means you are using it faster than time passes.
dataAI: AI limits, if you turn them on
